links.outcome: Physician Top-3 diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: Adjusted Top-3 accuracy 62.3% unassisted vs 74.6% AI-assisted (AOR 2.68, 95% CI 1.24 to 6.12; P=.01); Top-1 inconclusive (AOR 1.83, P=.08).
links.quote: Adjusted Top-3 diagnostic accuracy was 62.3% (95% CI 49.1% to 75.7%) in the unassisted condition and 74.6% (95% CI 63.7% to 85.4%) in the AI-assisted condition (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 2.68, 95% CI 1.24 to 6.12; χ21=6.4, P=.01).

links.outcome: Concordance with incorrect AI suggestions as a measure of overreliance
links.effect: With an incorrect operative AI suggestion, concordance was 38.8% unassisted vs 55.8% AI-assisted; not statistically significant (AOR 2.08, 95% CI 0.89 to 5.19; P=.09).
links.quote: In risk scenarios with an incorrect operative AI suggestion, adjusted concordance was 38.8% in the unassisted condition and 55.8% in the AI-assisted condition, but the between-condition comparison was not statistically significant (AOR 2.08, 95% CI 0.89 to 5.19; χ21=2.9, P=.09).

screen.reason: Randomized simulation trial evaluating physician diagnostic performance with vs without a real-time voice-based AI diagnostic assistant, measuring accuracy and overreliance.
